<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    We search for galaxy-scale (Dysonian) waste heat in the mid-infrared using WISE. Starting from the 2MASS Redshift Survey, we crossmatch to CatWISE2020 and AllWISE, apply standard MIR AGN/starburst vetoes (Stern, Assef R90, Jarrett), and treat W1 and W2 as stellar baselines and W3 and W4 as constraining bands. For each galaxy and for blackbody waste heat temperatures
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    = 150–600 K, we convert W3/W4 photometry into conservative 3
                    <jats:italic>σ</jats:italic>
                    per-galaxy upper limits on the bolometric waste heat luminosity using the WISE bandpass color correction. The resulting distributions have median caps of ∼(5–9) × 10
                    <jats:sup>8</jats:sup>
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    across
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    = 150–600 K. Aggregated at the
                    <jats:italic>population</jats:italic>
                    level, the one-sided 95% upper bound on the fraction of nearby galaxies that could host waste heat above a given threshold monotonically decreases with threshold and asymptotes to  ≃1/6500 at high thresholds (set by the sample size). Sensitivity transitions from W4 at
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    ≲ 200 K to W3 at
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    ≳ 300 K. Interpreted with the AGENT formalism, a fiducial Milky Way like stellar luminosity
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⋆</jats:sub>
                    = 3 × 10
                    <jats:sup>10</jats:sup>
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    implies typical per galaxy caps of
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                    ≡
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>wh</jats:sub>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⋆</jats:sub>
                    ≲ 1.7%–2.9% over
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    = 150–600 K (e.g.,
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                    ≲ 1.8% at
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    = 300 K). At
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    ≃ 300 K, no more than
                    <jats:italic>f</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>95</jats:sub>
                    ≃ 1.61 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4</jats:sup>
                    ( ≃0.0161%) of nearby galaxies can host KIII-scale systems reprocessing ≳21% of a Milky-Way-like stellar luminosity into ∼300 K waste heat.
                  </jats:p>
title: WISE/CatWISE Constraints on Dysonian Waste-heat Technosignatures in Nearby Galaxies
